## Principal component anaylisis in diabetes data set

### Introduction

The data consist of 19 variables on 403 subjects from 1046 subjects who were interviewed in a study to understand the prevalence of obesity, diabetes, and other cardiovascular risk factors in central Virginia for African Americans. According to Dr John Hong, Diabetes Mellitus Type II (adult onset diabetes) is associated most strongly with obesity. The 403 subjects were the ones who were actually screened for diabetes. Glycosolated hemoglobin \> 7.0 is usually taken as a positive diagnosis of diabetes.

The aim of this micro-report is to establish if there are any determining factors for diabetes diagnosis. Only cholesterol, glucose level, HDL, ratio and glycosolated hemoglobin are considered to perform PCA.

### Loading the data & initializing the libraries

```{r}
library("tidyverse")
library("broom")
library("cowplot")
```

We are going to be working with the diabetes data set. The objective of this micro-report is finding out which out of all the possible variables determine the possibility of diabetes.

```{r}
diabetes <- read_csv("data/diabetes.csv")
```

### Re-structuring the data

```{r}
diabetes <- diabetes |>
  select('chol', 'stab.glu', 'hdl', 'ratio', 'glyhb') |>
  mutate(diagnosis = case_when(
    glyhb >= 7 ~ "diabetic",
    glyhb < 7 ~ "not_diabetic"
  ))
```
